items.X_desc: Score 0-10 how much the post positions itself as unfinished or in need of confirmation: direct questions to readers ('Does this work?', 'Can someone please explain why ... is incorrect?', 'Wouldn't that be overcounting?', 'Did anyone else miss this?'), hedged self-report of a result ('I'm getting ...', 'I think ...', 'I hope it is valid'), a narrated attempt that stops before finishing, and admissions of a gap or an abandoned computation. 0 = the post asserts its content flatly with no appeal to the reader; 10 = it is principally a request for help or reassurance. Do NOT judge whether the uncertainty is warranted, humble or annoying, and do NOT decide whether the mathematics is correct. Score only the extent of the visible uncertainty posture.
items.Y_desc: Read only the post text. Score 0-10 the EXTENT to which the author uses self-deprecating, hedging, or uncertainty-signaling language about their own solution or competence (e.g. 'not sure', 'I sure do hope it is valid', 'scuffed', 'oversimplified', 'cheap', admissions of confusion, sad/frustrated emoticons). 0 = no such language anywhere; 10 = pervasive self-deprecation or hedging throughout the post. Do NOT judge whether the solution is actually good, rigorous, or correctly hedged -- score only how much of this self-referential hedging language is present in the text.

items.X_name: Back-reference language presupposing earlier posts in the thread
items.X_desc: Read only the problem and this one post. Score 0-10 how much of the post's language presupposes that other posts already exist in this thread and positions this post relative to them. Count: direct address to another poster ('@above', 'thanks!', 'his monovariant'); phrases such as 'similar to above', 'different from the others', 'I already addressed this in my previous post', 'as I said', 'the wiki solution #2', 'Solution 2', 'another way'; a reply that continues an argument the reader cannot see; and any sentence that would be incoherent if this were the first post. 0 = the post engages the bare problem as though nothing had been said yet; 10 = nearly every sentence leans on unseen prior posts. You must NOT judge whether back-reference is good, polite, helpful or lazy, must NOT judge the mathematics, and must NOT try to guess what the earlier posts said. Score only the visible extent of back-reference language.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for how much the post explicitly presupposes or references other entries in the thread, such as earlier solutions, numbered solutions, or replies; do not judge whether this feature is good.

items.X_desc: Score 0-10 the extent to which the post uses insider community shorthand without explanation -- e.g. 'WLOG', 'FTSOC', 'Let P(x,y) denote the assertion', named recurring-trick labels like 'pointwise trap', forum-specific emoticons (e.g. :yoda:, :blacksquare:). 0 = no such shorthand, everything spelled out in plain language; 10 = jargon-dense throughout. Do not judge whether the jargon is used correctly or reflects real expertise -- score only how much of this shorthand vocabulary appears.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for how much the post uses compressed insider conventions, unexplained shorthand, routine assertion labels, or dense expert-to-expert prose; do not judge whether this feature is good.

items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for how much the post explicitly labels the problem as easy, hard, routine, contest-specific, school-level, or otherwise places it in a venue or difficulty category. Judge only the presence of such labels; do not judge whether they are good.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 the extent to which the post labels its own solution with qualitative descriptors such as 'cheap', 'fast', 'overkill', 'scuffed', 'troll', 'cursed', 'different', 'alternative', or 'simple'. Do not judge whether the label is accurate; score only how many such self-assessment phrases appear.

items.X_desc: Score 0–10 for the extent of explicit references to collaborators, helpers, prior assistance, or thanking another participant; do not judge the value of that assistance.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the extent of visible social-network residue, including usernames, @-replies, collaboration credits, thanks, or comments about other contributors. Judge only visible text; do not judge whether this feature is good.

items.X_desc: Score 0-10 the extent to which the post uses structured presentation macros: [color=...] tags, bolded/labeled 'Claim'/'Proof'/'Lemma' headers, numbered section headers (e.g. '1. ...', '2. ...'), or repeated boxed-answer formatting used as a structuring device. 0 = plain unstructured prose with none of these; 10 = heavy, systematic use of colored/labeled/numbered macro structure throughout. Do not judge whether the structure is helpful or well-organized -- score only how much of this specific markup vocabulary appears.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the extent of deliberate forum-format conventions such as hide blocks, colored headings, claim/proof labels, list tags, display structure, or boxed conclusions. Judge only formatting presence; do not judge whether it is good.

items.X_desc: Score 0-10 the extent to which the post frames itself by the circumstances of its own production rather than by its content: statements that this was written during or just after the contest, references to a score or grade received, worry about points lost, elapsed solving time, comparisons to other problems on the same paper, and named co-solvers or credited collaborators ('Solved with ...', a bolded handle). 0 = no such framing anywhere; 10 = the post is dominated by it. Do NOT judge whether such framing is impressive, boastful or irrelevant, and do NOT treat any claimed score or timing as evidence of anything. Score only how much production-circumstance framing is visible.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 the extent to which the post explicitly credits or mentions other forum users as collaborators or co-solvers (e.g., 'Solved with [user]', 'thanks to [user]'). Do not judge whether collaboration is good; score only how much attribution to others appears.

items.X_name: Tutorial-report register with numbered bolded section headings
items.X_desc: Score 0-10 how much the post is organised as a formal report for a reader rather than as a working write-up: numbered and bolded section headings that name stages ('1. The Strategy', '2. Constructing ...', 'Conclusion'), a restatement of the goal before each stage, explicit signposting ('We now prove that', 'Let us evaluate', 'This implies that'), every routine algebraic step spelled out rather than compressed, and a closing paragraph that restates what was shown. 0 = no sectioning or signposting at all; 10 = fully sectioned, signposted and summarised. Do NOT judge whether this organisation is clear, bloated or professional, and do NOT judge the mathematics. Score only the extent of the report scaffolding.

Do not judge whether references are appropriate.

A high score means most equations are displayed prominently; a low score means most math is inline. Do not judge whether display math is better; score only the ratio.

items.X_name: Multiple-choice answer-extraction framing in the post
items.X_desc: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the post is written as the extraction of one lettered option rather than as a free-standing argument: it names or boxes an answer letter (\boxed{\textbf{(C)}}, 'Choice (E) is obviously false', 'so the answer must be (C) 36'), it reasons over the option list itself ('the only answer choice that is odd and 1 mod 3', 'the answer choices are all clearly distinct', 'the choices are furthermore all real'), it appeals to the answer being one of five, or it plugs candidate options back in. Also count lighter traces: a final numeric value asserted with no proof obligation, or an explicit remark that the shortcut suffices because only the option must be identified. 0 = the post never behaves as though a fixed option list exists and argues to an unconditioned conclusion; 10 = the option list is the organising device of the whole post. Score only how much option-directed framing is present. You must NOT judge whether shortcutting to the letter is legitimate or whether the reasoning is sound.
items.Y_desc: Score 0-10 for the extent to which the post foregrounds answer choices, option letters, boxed numerical outputs, or answer-checking language. Judge only this assessment-format trace; do not judge whether it is good.

Do not judge whether such commentary is useful.
